original_pre_race_assessment.raw_reasoning:
The novice winner steps into a five-runner handicap against demonstrated handicap hurdle form around this trip. Washington has just beaten Handlethekettle by 3.5 lengths, and both provide a concrete alternative to simply projecting Mwabani’s next improvement.

Winning case: Mwabani won his Chepstow novice by 4.75 lengths, has three earlier seconds, and can progress from an opening handicap mark of 115. The longer trip may help. A new condition is not proven inability.

Decision: Recommend the strong-competition route at 5.10. The decision rests on established, relevant hurdle opposition, not a claim that 115 is necessarily harsh or that the favourite cannot stay. Washington’s rating edge is largely paid for in weight; there is no automatic pounds advantage.

Ranked rivals:
1. Washington: Wetherby winner over 2m3f154y, beating Handlethekettle 3.5 lengths at equal gross weights. Now concedes that rival 5 lb and Mwabani 13 lb after a 5 lb rise; may still reproduce the strongest recent handicap performance, but is ten and can race keenly.
2. Handlethekettle: Worcester and Wetherby runner-up with a previous Class 2 hurdle win. Receives 5 lb from Washington after meeting level previously, providing a supported reversal route, although jumping errors and the prior defeat remain material.
3. Treasure Planet: Chepstow handicap winner and Newbury seventh, beaten 7.5 lengths cumulatively, not 1.25 lengths. An improving four-year-old on 159 lb; the latest run was respectable rather than a second independent major negative. Son Of Hypnos has 135 lb after the 7 lb claim but comes from weaker company.

original_pre_race_assessment.raw_reasoning:
Recent 5f winning and placed evidence from One For Harvey gives a specific rival to Lazzar, whose latest current-yard runs have not restored his earlier level. La Belle Forest adds actual recent 5f form; this is more than several hypothetical revivals.

Winning case: Lazzar is a four-time AW winner and his mark is 16 lb below his last winning rating. He was only a length behind the winner at Southwell and 1.75 lengths behind at Kempton. A revival at this level is credible; those two runs are not heavy defeats.

Decision: Pick at 5.00. One For Harvey’s recent win and follow-up third on equal 134 lb today make the opposition persuasive despite Lazzar’s reduced mark. The decision does not assume an automatic draw or pace disadvantage, and the favourite’s revival could still win.

Ranked rivals:
1. One For Harvey: Won over 5f at Southwell, then third beaten 0.75 length from a 6 lb higher mark; another 1 lb higher now. Carries 134 lb, same as Lazzar, with no current claim. Draw 10 and the change from Tapeta to Polytrack limit transfer.
2. La Belle Forest: Third at Wolverhampton over 5f, beaten 1.25 lengths, now 131 lb off 57. Better settling helped, but earlier inconsistency means repeating it is uncertain.
3. Diamond Dreamer: Two recent fourths show competitive form off a reduced mark, 131 lb today. The latest was 6f and he has a long losing sequence; rank behind the two more direct 5f routes. Little Jaybee’s last-run concern and Davorge Nation’s possible progress are included, not counted as established extra threats.

original_pre_race_assessment.raw_reasoning:
There is actual late weakening over this course and distance on 27 April, when fourth beaten 6.75 lengths, together with staying opposition headed by Noble Grace. This is a trip-specific concern, not merely an untried trip or a poor form figure.

Winning case: In The Post returned with a Kempton third after a break and is now rated 57, 5 lb below the April course-and-distance attempt. He can be fitter and may stay better under different race conditions. The April run alone does not prove an absolute stamina limit.

Decision: Strongest of the three Picks at 5.50. Noble Grace’s proven staying route is enough to support opposition; Calshot Spit adds Flat stamina. Chilli King is explicitly an improvement possibility, not a third proven stayer. The lower-mark/fitness case does not erase the specific earlier run.

Ranked rivals:
1. Noble Grace: Won over 2m2f at Pontefract, then third over 2m at Kempton, beaten 1.25 lengths. Carries 140 lb versus the selection’s 134 lb, broadly reflecting the 6 lb rating gap; no automatic weight advantage. Cheekpieces return, but running in snatches and race execution are limitations.
2. Calshot Spit: Second over 2m1f at Bath on the Flat, beaten 9 lengths; his recent fourth at Lingfield was a hurdle race, not a Flat form boost. 136 lb less 3 lb = 133 lb. Long absence from AW creates transfer uncertainty.
3. Chilli King: Lightly raced and met trouble in running when fifth over 1m6f at Southwell, beaten 4 lengths. A longer trip can help but is not demonstrated stamina. Notable Charm’s staying placings and Autumn’s Breeze’s class-drop/blinkers revival are substantial whole-field alternatives.
